title: Homestead — Energy
description: Energy-management view (SDD sections 13, 30-38). Every panel reads a table the platform actually writes: energy_state_snapshot, energy_state_transitions, load_shed_actions, power_load_profiles, telemetry_samples and current_state. Panels are empty until the EMS and the ingest path are running against a loaded registry — an empty panel here means no data, never a zero.

list.name: asset
list.label: Energy asset
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT asset_id FROM points WHERE asset_id LIKE 'energy.%' ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Energy operating state
panels.description: The single site energy state the EMS publishes. COMMISSIONING until the EMS has been enabled and has evaluated at least once.

targets.rawSql: SELECT state FROM energy_state_snapshot ORDER BY id LIMIT 1

panels.title: Input data quality
panels.description: SDD 30.5: the state machine must not act on invalid measurements. 'degraded' or 'bad' means the EMS is operating conservatively, not that the plant is healthy.

targets.rawSql: SELECT data_quality FROM energy_state_snapshot ORDER BY id LIMIT 1

panels.title: Generator request
panels.description: SDD 34: the EMS requests, the generator controller decides. This is the request, not the generator's actual state.

targets.rawSql: SELECT generator_request FROM energy_state_snapshot ORDER BY id LIMIT 1

panels.title: Since last EMS evaluation
panels.description: A rising number means the EMS tick has stopped. The energy state shown above is then stale and must not be trusted.

targets.rawSql: SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - last_evaluated_at)) AS age_s FROM energy_state_snapshot ORDER BY id LIMIT 1

panels.title: Shed groups active
panels.description: SDD 32: number of load-shedding groups currently commanded off.

targets.rawSql: SELECT jsonb_array_length(COALESCE(shed_groups_active, '[]'::jsonb)) AS shed_groups FROM energy_state_snapshot ORDER BY id LIMIT 1

panels.title: Battery state of charge
panels.description: Point soc_pct from the historian. One series per asset (battery bank, BMS). Only samples with quality = 'good' are plotted; bad-quality samples appear in the data-quality table below rather than being drawn as if they were measurements.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts AS "time", asset_id AS metric, value_numeric FROM telemetry_samples WHERE point_name = 'soc_pct' AND quality = 'good' AND $__timeFilter(ts) ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Inverter DC input and AC output
panels.description: Points power_dc_input_kw and power_ac_output_kw. The design basis for array and inverter capacity is an unresolved conflict (SDD 30.2, open decision 22.1) — this panel plots what is measured, not what was designed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts AS "time", asset_id || ' dc_in' AS metric, value_numeric FROM telemetry_samples WHERE point_name = 'power_dc_input_kw' AND quality = 'good' AND $__timeFilter(ts) ORDER BY ts
SELECT ts AS "time", asset_id || ' ac_out' AS metric, value_numeric FROM telemetry_samples WHERE point_name = 'power_ac_output_kw' AND quality = 'good' AND $__timeFilter(ts) ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Site and panel load
panels.description: Points power_total_kw and power_ac_kw across energy assets — critical and general panels, meters, inverters.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts AS "time", asset_id || '/' || point_name AS metric, value_numeric FROM telemetry_samples WHERE point_name IN ('power_total_kw', 'power_ac_kw') AND quality = 'good' AND $__timeFilter(ts) ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Energy today and available reserve
panels.description: Points energy_today_kwh and energy_available_kwh. energy_available_kwh is a CALC point: it is the platform's derived reserve, not a meter reading.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts AS "time", asset_id || '/' || point_name AS metric, value_numeric FROM telemetry_samples WHERE point_name IN ('energy_today_kwh', 'energy_available_kwh') AND quality = 'good' AND $__timeFilter(ts) ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Load schedule by tier
panels.description: From power_load_profiles, populated by the EMS load-schedule loader. Tier 0 is physical protection and is never shed; tier 4 is opportunistic surplus. Rows are empty until data/load_schedule.yaml has been loaded (homestead-twin load-all).

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(effective_tier, base_tier) AS tier, name, asset_id, criticality, rated_power_kw AS rated_kw, estimated_power_kw AS estimated_kw, control_method, branch_circuit FROM power_load_profiles ORDER BY 1, name

panels.title: Shed and restore actions
panels.description: Every shed or restore the EMS attempted, with its outcome. SDD 32.3: a shed command that fails must be visible, not retried silently.

targets.rawSql: SELECT occurred_at, action, "group", asset_id, energy_state, outcome, reason FROM load_shed_actions WHERE $__timeFilter(occurred_at) ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 200

panels.title: Energy state transitions
panels.description: Append-only EMS history: what changed, what triggered it, and who or what asked. SDD 30.9 requires hysteresis and dwell — repeated fast transitions here mean the thresholds need work.

targets.rawSql: SELECT occurred_at, from_state, to_state, "trigger", actor, reason FROM energy_state_transitions WHERE $__timeFilter(occurred_at) ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 200

panels.title: Energy points that are stale or bad quality
panels.description: An energy dashboard that hides its own blind spots is worse than no dashboard. These are energy-domain points whose last value is not 'good', or older than the point's stale_after_s. SDD 26.6 and 30.5.

targets.rawSql: SELECT cs.point_id, cs.quality, cs.value_numeric, cs.unit, cs.ts, ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - cs.ts))::numeric, 0) AS age_s, cs.stale_after_s FROM current_state cs JOIN assets a ON a.asset_id = cs.asset_id WHERE a.domain = 'energy' AND (cs.quality <> 'good' OR cs.ts IS NULL OR (cs.stale_after_s IS NOT NULL AND cs.ts < now() - make_interval(secs => cs.stale_after_s))) ORDER BY cs.ts NULLS FIRST LIMIT 100

panels.title: What this dashboard does not show

options.content:
SDD section 38 also asks for **forecast reserve**, **PV curtailment**, **per-subsystem consumption attribution** and **cost/value modelling**. None of those are implemented, so none of them have a panel here. Adding an empty panel for an unimplemented value teaches the operator to ignore empty panels, and that habit is what makes a real gap invisible during an event.

Also absent, and deliberately: a **control** widget. Grafana is a read path. Commands go through the digital twin API so that every one of them carries a named operator, a reason, an idempotency key and an audit record (SDD 5.7, FR-004).

The **authoritative energy design is still an open conflict** (SDD 30.2, open decision 22.1): the older 12 kW / 40 kWh baseline versus the revised 45 kWdc / 800 kWh design. No threshold, axis maximum or reserve calculation on this dashboard assumes either one is correct.
